title: Flat quasi-finite purity across a depth-two source boundary
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be locally Noetherian schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] that is locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Let $W\subset X$ be open and assume that the composite $W\hookrightarrow X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume that for every $x\in X\setminus W$, $\operatorname{depth}(\mathcal O_{X,x})\geq2$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Then $f$ is etale. No normality, dominance, integrality, connectedness, or normalization setup is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BJH (Lemma 58.21.2), applied as in the proof of Tag 0EY6(3)

proof.text: For x outside W, the depth bound and depth at most local dimension show that x is not a generic point of a component. For any dimension-one generalization x' of x, the same depth bound would contradict dimension one if x' were outside W. Thus x' lies in W, where f is etale and hence unramified.

Apply the branch-locus argument of Tag 0BJH at x. Etale localization reduces the flat locally quasi-finite map to a finite locally free map with x the only point over y=f(x). The discriminant cuts out the locally principal ramification locus. If y were in that locus, a dimension-one generalization y' in it exists because x is not generic. A ramified point x' over y' specializes to x, since a finite map is closed and x is the only point over y. Finite flat local maps preserve dimension, so dim O(X,x')=1, contradicting the unramifiedness proved in the preceding step. Therefore f is etale at x. Points in W are already etale. Etaleness local on the source gives Etale f; empty X and W=X are included.
